html:
The Colombian peace process led to an agreement between the government of Juan Manuel Santos and the FARC guerrillas, signed in 2016, ending over fifty years of war.

Talks began in Havana in 2012. A first agreement, signed in Cartagena in September 2016, was narrowly rejected by voters in a referendum in October. A revised version was signed in November and approved by Congress. Santos won the Nobel Peace Prize that year. The FARC handed over its weapons to the United Nations in 2017.

The deal promised land reform, a special court for war crimes, and seats in Congress for the former rebels. Its promises were only partly kept: hundreds of social leaders and former fighters have been killed since, and other armed groups moved into old FARC areas. Still, it ended the largest war in Colombia's long conflict.
sum: The Colombian peace process led to an agreement between the government of Juan Manuel Santos and the FARC guerrillas, signed in 2016, ending over fifty years of war.
